reasoning: x divides x^3 and x^2 always, so x | (x^3+x^2+16) iff x | 16. Positive divisors of 16 are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 — exactly 5 values. Enumerated x=1..200 in python: {1,2,4,8,16}.
30 = 2·3·5, three distinct primes each to the first power. Each prime goes to exactly one of a, b, c, independently: 3^3 = 27 ordered triples. Brute-force count over a,b,c in 1..30 gives 27.
Real roots require discriminant 16 + 4·log10(N) >= 0, i.e. log10(N) >= -4, i.e. N >= 10^-4 = 1/10000. Minimum value is 1/10000.
Positive-integer solutions of x+y+z=12 number C(12-1, 3-1) = C(11,2) = 55. Brute-force enumeration confirms 55.

With a=n, b=n+1, c=n(n+1): I = n^2 + (n+1)^2 + n^2(n+1)^2 = (n^2+n+1)^2. Since n(n+1) is always even, n^2+n+1 is odd, so I is the square of an odd integer. Checked n=1..7: 9, 49, 169, 441, 961, 1849, 3249 = 3^2, 7^2, 13^2, 21^2, 31^2, 43^2, 57^2.

Smallest odd composite number is 9 (1 is not composite, 3/5/7 are prime). Digit sum of 23P62971335 is 41 + P; need 41+P divisible by 9, and 41 mod 9 = 5, so P = 4. Checked: 23462971335 / 9 = 2607005704 exactly.
Unit digits of powers of 3 cycle 3, 9, 7, 1 with period 4. 99 mod 4 = 3, so the unit digit is the third in the cycle, 7. pow(3,99,10) = 7.

LCM = 28·HCF and HCF + LCM = 1740 give 29·HCF = 1740, HCF = 60, LCM = 1680. Product of the numbers = HCF·LCM = 100800, so the other number = 100800/240 = 420. Verified gcd(240,420) = 60 and lcm(240,420) = 1680.
x^n - a^n = (x-a)(x^(n-1) + x^(n-2)a + ... + a^(n-1)) for every natural number n; the factorisation has no parity or primality restriction.
Rationalising, 1/(sqrt(k)+sqrt(k+1)) = sqrt(k+1) - sqrt(k). The sum telescopes from k=1 to 99 to sqrt(100) - sqrt(1) = 10 - 1 = 9. Numeric evaluation of the original sum gives 9.0.

Inner expression: sqrt(x) = x^(1/2); x·x^(1/2) = x^(3/2); sqrt of that = x^(3/4); x·x^(3/4) = x^(7/4). Taking the 14th root: x^(7/56) = x^(1/8), so m = 1/8. (Option D 7/4 is the exponent before the 14th root is applied — the distractor for dropping the radical index.)

For the ten numbers ±1..±5, sum = 0 and sum of squares = 2(1+4+9+16+25) = 110. Sum of pairwise products = ((sum)^2 - sum of squares)/2 = (0 - 110)/2 = -55. Direct enumeration over all 45 pairs also gives -55.
Speed 132 km/hr = 132000/3600 = 110/3 m/s. Distance to clear the bridge = 110 + 165 = 275 m. Time = 275/(110/3) = 825/110 = 7.5 seconds.
SI = P/4 and SI = P·R·T/100 with R = T = n gives P·n^2/100 = P/4, so n^2 = 25, n = 5 (positive root).
Writing space is constant: 60n = (60+10)(n-3) = 70(n-3). So 60n = 70n - 210, giving 10n = 210, n = 21.
x men × x hours/day × x days = x^3 man-hours produce x units, so the rate is 1/x^2 units per man-hour. y men × y hours/day × y days = y^3 man-hours produce k = y^3/x^2 = y^3·x^(-2) units.
d(5) = 2, d(11) = 2, d(55) = 4, d(16) = 5. Statement 1: 2 = 2, true. Statement 2: 2·2 = 4 = d(55), true. Statement 3: 2+2 = 4, but d(16) = 5, false. So 1 and 2 only.

Statement 1 is false: A_1 = 2+1 = 3 is prime (also A_2 = 7, A_3 = 31, A_4 = 211, A_5 = 2311 are all prime). Statement 2: P_n is even for every n>=1 (it contains the factor 2), so A_n + 2 = P_n + 3 is odd — true. Statement 3: A_n + 1 = P_n + 2 is even — true. So 2 and 3 only.

The balance shows 1000 g for an actual 800 g, so the customer pays the cost price of 1000 g but receives only 800 g. Taking cost c per gram: outlay 800c, receipt 1000c, profit 200c on cost 800c = 25%.
Flow speed 2 km/hr = 2000/60 = 100/3 m per minute. Volume per minute = 3 m × 40 m × 100/3 m = 4000 m^3 = 4000 × 1000 = 40,00,000 litres.
With cost price C: x = 0.72C (28% loss) and y = 1.12C (12% profit). y/x = 1.12/0.72 = 112/72 = 14/9.
300/v - 300/(v+15) = 1 gives 4500 = v^2 + 15v, so v^2 + 15v - 4500 = 0 with roots 60 and -75. The positive root is 60 km/hr. Check: 300/60 = 5 h, 300/75 = 4 h, a difference of 1 h.

Put x = ky. (1) (x^2+y^2)/(x^2-y^2) = (k^2+1)/(k^2-1), a constant, so x^2+y^2 varies as x^2-y^2 — true. (2) x/y^2 = k/y, so it varies inversely as y — true. (3) x^4y^2 = (x^2y)^2, so (x^4y^2)^(1/(2n)) = (x^2y)^(1/n); the two quantities are identical (ratio 1 verified numerically for n = 2, 3, 5) — true. All three.
Ena is 13; mother = 13 + 24 = 37; father = 37 + 3 = 40. Ena was born 4 years after the marriage, so the marriage was 13 + 4 = 17 years ago. Father's age then = 40 - 17 = 23 years.
Mahesh 60; Ram = 60 - 5 = 55; Raju = 55 - 4 = 51; Babu = 51 - 6 = 45. Difference between Mahesh and Babu = 60 - 45 = 15 years.
Final count = N(1 + x/100)(1 - x/100) = N(1 - x^2/10000) = N - Nx^2/10000, which is strictly less than N for any x > 0, independently of N.
From ab + xy - xb = 0: ab = x(b - y), so x/a = b/(b - y). From bc + yz - cy = 0: c(b - y) = -yz, so c/z = -y/(b - y). Sum = (b - y)/(b - y) = 1. Confirmed by sympy substitution.

Product of the polynomials = HCF × LCM. LCM factors as (3x+1)(5x-3)(2x+1) and the given polynomial is (3x+1)(2x+1). Other = (3x+1)(30x^3+7x^2-10x-3)/(6x^2+5x+1) = (3x+1)(5x-3) = 15x^2 - 4x - 3. Verified: gcd with 6x^2+5x+1 is 3x+1 and lcm is the given LCM.
Subtracting the two equations gives 4(2q - 1) = 0, so q = 1/2 and 2q - 1 = 0. Then the left side of either equation is 0, so 2pq - 10 = 0 and pq = 5. (Unique solution p = 10, q = 1/2 from sympy.)

Term 1 = a(a+c)/(c(a-c)(a+c)) = a/(c(a-c)); term 2 = (a-c)(a+c)/(c(a+c)^2) = (a-c)/(c(a+c)); term 3 = 2c/((a-c)(a+c)); term 4 = 3/(a+c). Combining gives 6/(a+c). Sympy simplify returns 6/(a+c); numeric check a=5, c=2 gives 6/7 = 6/(a+c).
(2x^2 + 2x - 1)^2 = 4x^4 + 8x^3 + 4x^2 - 4x^2 - 4x + 1 = 4x^4 + 8x^3 - 4x + 1, an exact match. The other three options were squared and none matches.

(10a + b) - (10b + a) = 9(a - b) = 27 gives a - b = 3; with a + b = 13 this gives a = 8, b = 5. The number is 85 and the product of the digits is 40. Exhaustive search over two-digit numbers yields only (8, 5).
Setting each ratio to k: x = k(b+c), y = k(c+a), z = k(b-a). Then x - y - z = k[(b+c) - (c+a) - (b-a)] = k·0 = 0. The other options give 2k(b+c), 2k(a+c) and k(4b+3c-a), none identically zero.

Take X's start as t = 0, so X is at 4t. Y starts at t = 2 and overtakes when 4t = 5(t-2), i.e. t = 10. Z must overtake at the same instant t = 10: 4(10) = 6(10 - s) gives s = 10/3, so Z starts at t = 10/3. That is 10/3 - 2 = 4/3 hours after Y.

1 - x - x^n + x^(n+1) = (1 - x) - x^n(1 - x) = (1 - x)(1 - x^n), and 1 - x^n = (1 - x)(1 + x + ... + x^(n-1)). So the expression has (1 - x)^2 as a factor. Polynomial remainder modulo (1-x)^2 is 0 for n = 1..6.

Profit = 75 - x and it equals x% of the outlay x, i.e. x^2/100. So x^2 + 100x - 7500 = 0, with positive root x = 50. Check: cost 50, profit 25 = 50% of 50, selling price 75. (The options carry '%' signs although x is a rupee cost — the intended numeric answer is 50.)

value: x(t - y) t y^(-1), i.e. xt(t-y)/y km
reasoning: Distance D, original speed D/t, new speed D/(t-y) = D/t + x. So D/(t-y) - D/t = x gives Dy/(t(t-y)) = x, hence D = xt(t-y)/y = x(t-y)·t·y^(-1). Sympy solve returns t·x·(t-y)/y. NOTE ON THE WORDING (verified against page p07 of the booklet, which reads exactly as transcribed): 'How long was the journey?' reads as if it asks for the TIME, which the stem has already given as t hours. All four printed options have the dimensions of a distance (km/hr × hr = km), so 'how long' must mean the distance travelled, and that is what is derived here. Solved as printed; no option corresponds to a time.
t proportional to sqrt(d), so t2 = 4·sqrt(122.50/78.40) = 4·sqrt(1.5625) = 4 × 1.25 = 5 seconds. (Exact ratio 12250/7840 = 25/16.)

Taking log10 with the supplied values log6 = 0.778, log4 = 0.602, log8 = 0.903: (3-4x)(0.778) + (x+5)(0.602) = 0.903 gives 5.344 - 2.510x = 0.903, so x = 4.441/2.510 = 1.7693. Solving exactly with natural logs gives x = 1.76920, the same interval. So 1 < x < 2.
The Euclidean algorithm repeatedly replaces (a, b) by (b, a mod b) and terminates at the greatest common divisor, i.e. the HCF of two integers.

For rational r > 0, surface area 4*pi*r^2 and volume (4/3)*pi*r^3 are both a non-zero rational multiple of pi, and pi is irrational, so neither is rational. Sympy confirms is_rational is False for both with r = 3.

m = cosec θ - sin θ = cos^2θ/sinθ and n = sec θ - cos θ = sin^2θ/cosθ. Then mn = sinθ cosθ, and m^(2/3) + n^(2/3) = (cos^2θ + sin^2θ)/(sinθcosθ)^(2/3) = 1/(sinθcosθ)^(2/3). The expression is (mn)^(2/3)(m^(2/3) + n^(2/3)) = (sinθcosθ)^(2/3) · (sinθcosθ)^(-2/3) = 1. Numeric check at θ = 1/7, 1/3, 4/5, 0.3, 1.1 rad all give 1.000000.

With c = cos θ, sin^2θ - tan^2θ = (1-c^2)(1 - 1/c^2) = -(1-c^2)^2/c^2 = -(c^2 + 1/c^2 - 2). Since k^2 = c^2 + 2 + 1/c^2, we get c^2 + 1/c^2 - 2 = k^2 - 4, so the expression is 4 - k^2. Numeric check at θ = 0.3, 0.7, 1.2, 2.0, 2.5 rad matches 4 - k^2 to 15 digits (and is the negative of option C throughout).
An angle in a semicircle is a right angle, so angle C = 90 degrees and A + B = 90 degrees. Then cos(A+B) + sin(A+B) = cos 90 + sin 90 = 0 + 1 = 1.

For real x != 0, x + 1/x - 2 = (x-1)^2/x >= 0 when x > 0 and x + 1/x + 2 = (x+1)^2/x <= 0 when x < 0, so x + 1/x lies in (-inf, -2] U [2, inf). Both sin θ and cos θ lie in [-1, 1], so neither equation is possible. Numeric scan over 800,000 values of x confirms |x + 1/x| >= 2 always.
Interior angle of a regular n-gon = (n-2)·180/n degrees; for n = 5 that is 108 degrees = 108·pi/180 = 3*pi/5 radians.
Sum = 5*pi/12 rad = 75 degrees, difference = 15 degrees. So the angles are 45 and 30 degrees, and k = 45/30 = 3/2.

Statement 1: 2sin^2θ - cosθ + 4 = 0 becomes 2c^2 + c - 6 = 0 with c = cos θ, whose roots are c = 3/2 and c = -2, both outside [-1, 1] — so the equation holds for NO θ, let alone all θ; false. Statement 2: for 0 < θ < pi/2, tanθ + cotθ >= 2 by AM-GM (sympy minimum on the open interval returns 2); true. So 2 only.
Central angle 42 degrees = 42 × (22/7)/180 = 11/15 radian. Arc s = r·θ gives r = 44/(11/15) = 44 × 15/11 = 60 m.
sin θ has maximum 1, so 3 sin θ - 4 has maximum 3 - 4 = -1. Sympy maximum confirms -1.

Squaring sinθ + cosθ = sqrt(2) gives 1 + 2 sinθcosθ = 2, so sinθcosθ = 1/2 and sin^2θcos^2θ = 1/4. sin^6 + cos^6 = 1 - 3 sin^2cos^2 = 1 - 3/4 = 1/4; adding 6 sin^2cos^2 = 3/2 gives 1/4 + 3/2 = 7/4. Direct evaluation at θ = pi/4 gives 7/4.
9 sin^2θ + 16 cos^2θ = 9(sin^2 + cos^2) + 7 cos^2θ = 9 + 7cos^2θ, minimised at cos θ = 0, giving 9. Sympy minimum confirms 9.

cos^2 47 - sin^2 47 = (cos47 - sin47)(cos47 + sin47) = k(cos47 - sin47). Since k^2 = 1 + 2 sin47 cos47, (cos47 - sin47)^2 = 2 - k^2; and because 47 > 45 degrees, sin47 > cos47 so cos47 - sin47 is negative, giving -sqrt(2-k^2). Hence the value is -k·sqrt(2-k^2). Numerically k = 1.4133520617 and cos^2 47 - sin^2 47 = -0.06975647374, matching -k·sqrt(2-k^2) exactly to 30 digits (option A has the wrong sign, option C is imaginary here).

p^3 = cosec θ - sin θ = cos^2θ/sinθ and q^3 = sec θ - cos θ = sin^2θ/cosθ. Then q^3/p^3 = (sin^2θ/cosθ)·(sinθ/cos^2θ) = tan^3θ, so tan θ = q/p. Numeric check at θ = 0.4, 0.9, 1.3 rad: q/p equals tan θ to 15 digits in every case.
With 0 <= α, β <= 90 degrees, α - β lies in [-90, 90], and cos(α - β) = 1 forces α - β = 0, i.e. α = β. Then sinα - sinβ + cosα - cosβ = 0.

Statement 1: sin 29 = cos 61, so the sum is 2 cos 61 = 0.9696..., which does not exceed 1 — true. Statement 2: cot 67 = tan 23, so tan 23 - cot 67 = 0 exactly (sympy simplify returns 0), which is not less than 0 — false. So 1 only.

With angle B = 90, Pythagoras in triangle ABC gives AC^2 = AB^2 + BC^2. Substituting into AB^2 + BC^2 + CD^2 - AD^2 = 0 gives AC^2 + CD^2 = AD^2, so triangle ACD is right-angled at C and angle ACD = 90 degrees. Verified numerically: for A(0,3), B(0,0), C(4,0) and D on the perpendicular to AC at C, the identity holds exactly for every choice of CD.
The internal bisector from A divides BC in the ratio of the adjacent sides: BD/DC = AB/AC = 16/12 = 4/3. With BD = 4, DC = 4 × 3/4 = 3 cm.

P, Q, R, S all lie on the same circle, and taking A, B, C, D in order the bisector feet occur in the cyclic order P, Q, R, S (P is the midpoint of arc BCD, Q of arc CDA, R of arc DAB, S of arc ABC). PQRS is therefore a cyclic quadrilateral and angle PQR and angle RSP are its opposite angles, summing to 180 degrees. Numerically checked on three different cyclic quadrilaterals: the sum was 180.000000 in each.

Side a, BD = a/3. Cosine rule in triangle ABD with angle B = 60 degrees: AD^2 = a^2 + a^2/9 - 2·a·(a/3)·(1/2) = 7a^2/9. So AD^2 : AB^2 = 7 : 9. Coordinate check with A(1/2, sqrt3/2), B(0,0), C(1,0), D = B + (C-B)/3 gives AD^2 = 7/9.

In trapezium ABCD with AB parallel to CD, the diagonals meet at O and triangles AOB, COD are similar (AA, from the alternate angles), so AO/OC = BO/OD — statement 1 is true. A line parallel to the two parallel sides is parallel to both, so by the basic proportionality theorem applied in the triangles formed by a diagonal it cuts the non-parallel sides in the same ratio — statement 2 is true.

With V = (1/3)pi r^2 H and C = pi r l where l^2 = r^2 + H^2: 3 pi V H^3 = pi^2 r^2 H^4 and 9V^2 = pi^2 r^4 H^2, so the sum is pi^2 r^2 H^2 (H^2 + r^2) = pi^2 r^2 l^2 H^2 = C^2 H^2. Sympy gives the ratio (3 pi V H^3 + 9V^2)/(C^2 H^2) = 1 identically.
Big ball radius 8 cm = 80 mm; small balls have diameter 2 mm, i.e. radius 1 mm. Volume ratio = (80/1)^3 = 512000 balls.
Third side = 90 - 40 - 41 = 9 cm, s = 45. Heron: sqrt(45·5·4·36) = sqrt(32400) = 180 cm^2. Cross-check: 9^2 + 40^2 = 1681 = 41^2, so it is right-angled and the area is (1/2)(9)(40) = 180.

Let the diagonals be d and d+2. Side = sqrt(d^2 + (d+2)^2)/2 and perimeter = 2 sqrt(d^2+(d+2)^2). Setting perimeter = sum of diagonals + 6 gives 2 sqrt(2d^2+4d+4) = 2d + 8, i.e. d^2 - 4d - 12 = 0, so d = 6. Diagonals 6 and 8, side 5, perimeter 20, sum of diagonals 14, difference exactly 6. Area = (1/2)(6)(8) = 24 square units.

In a right-angled triangle the circumcentre is the midpoint of the hypotenuse, so the hypotenuse = 2 × 5 = 10 cm. Taking the hypotenuse as base with the given altitude 4 cm, area = (1/2)(10)(4) = 20 cm^2. The configuration is possible since the maximum altitude to the hypotenuse is half the hypotenuse = 5 > 4.

Splitting 180 in the given ratios: 1:2:3 -> 30, 60, 90; 3:4:5 -> 45, 60, 75; 5:6:7 -> 50, 60, 70 — all integers. But 6:7:8 has parts summing to 21 and 180/21 = 60/7, giving 360/7, 60, 480/7, which are not integers. So 6 : 7 : 8 cannot be the proportion.
New area factor = 1.10 × 0.90 = 0.99, i.e. 99/100 of the original — a decrease of 1%.
Surface area ratio 1:4 gives radius ratio sqrt(1/4) = 1:2, and volume scales as the cube of the radius, so the volume ratio is 1 : 8.
Sum of exterior angles is 360 for any polygon, so (n-2)·180 = 2 × 360 = 720, giving n - 2 = 4 and n = 6 — a hexagon.
11 km = 1,100,000 cm over 5000 revolutions gives a circumference of 220 cm. With 2*pi*r = 220 and pi = 22/7, r = 220 × 7/44 = 35 cm.
Diameters 4:5 give radii 4:5. Since V is proportional to r^2 h, (16/25)(h1/h2) = 1/4, so h1/h2 = 25/64, i.e. the heights are in the ratio 25 : 64.
Setting 2A = 3B = 6C = k gives A = k/2, B = k/3, C = k/6; their sum k(1/2 + 1/3 + 1/6) = k = 180, so A = 90, B = 60, C = 30. Hence A + C = 120 degrees.
Equal perimeters: 2*pi*r = 4a gives a = pi*r/2. Ratio of areas = pi r^2 : (pi r/2)^2 = pi r^2 : pi^2 r^2/4 = 1 : pi/4 = 4 : pi. Sympy confirms the ratio equals 4/pi.

Consecutive even integers m, m+2, m+4 with m^2 + (m+2)^2 = (m+4)^2 gives m^2 - 4m - 12 = 0, so m = 6: the triangle is 6, 8, 10. Product = 6 × 8 × 10 = 480. Exhaustive search over even m up to 200 finds only (6, 8, 10).
The radii to the points of contact are perpendicular to the tangents, so in quadrilateral AMON angle AMO = angle ANO = 90 degrees. Hence angle MON = 360 - 70 - 90 - 90 = 110 degrees.
For a right-angled triangle a^2 + b^2 = c^2, so the sum of the squares of all three sides is 2c^2 = 8450, giving c^2 = 4225 and c = 65 units.
Equal bases b and equal areas: (1/2)·b·h_triangle = b·h_parallelogram, so h_triangle = 2·h_parallelogram and k = 2.
Areas are in the ratio m^2 : n^4, so the sides are in the ratio sqrt(m^2) : sqrt(n^4) = m : n^2. Perimeter is 4 × side, so the perimeters are in the same ratio m : n^2.

value: Area of triangle PAB is equal to area of triangle PAC
reasoning: AD is a median, so [ABD] = [ACD] (equal bases BD = DC, common apex A) and [PBD] = [PCD] (equal bases, common apex P). Subtracting, [PAB] = [PAC]. Numeric check with A(0.3,4.1), B(-2,0), C(5,0.7) and P at four positions along AD: the two areas agree exactly each time.

Segment area = sector area - triangle area = (1/2)r^2*theta - (1/2)r^2*sin(theta) = (1/2)r^2(theta - sin theta). Since sin theta = 2 sin(theta/2) cos(theta/2), this is option B; sympy gives the difference between them as exactly 0.

With the right angle at C: AQ^2 = AC^2 + CQ^2 and BP^2 = BC^2 + CP^2, so AQ^2 + BP^2 = (AC^2 + BC^2) + (CQ^2 + CP^2) = AB^2 + PQ^2 — statement 1 is true (verified numerically at four (P,Q) positions). Statement 2 is false: with C(0,0), A(0,6), B(8,0), AB = 10 while 2PQ took the values 7.343, 8.736, 20.000 and 14.400 for different P, Q. So 1 only.

Coins at the vertices touching their neighbours means the square has side 2r. The four quarter-circles inside the square total one full circle, so the uncovered area is 4r^2 - pi*r^2 = r^2(4 - 22/7) = 6r^2/7 = 42, giving r^2 = 49 and r = 7 cm.
The bucket is a frustum with radii x and 2x and height 3x. Volume = (1/3)*pi*h*(R^2 + Rr + r^2) = (1/3)(22/7)(3x)(4x^2 + 2x^2 + x^2) = (22/7)(7x^3) = 22x^3.
s = 2(pq + qr + rp) and t = pqr, so 1/p + 1/q + 1/r = (qr + rp + pq)/pqr = (s/2)/t = s/(2t). Verified identically by sympy.

Fifteen candidates sat the exam and only ten marks are printed, so five candidates failed and their marks are not printed — the stem still asks for the median of all fifteen. Any failing mark is at most the lowest pass mark 4, so in the sorted list of fifteen the five unknown marks occupy positions 1-5 and the printed marks 4, 5, 6, 6, 7, 7, 8, 8, 9, 9 occupy positions 6-15. The median is the 8th value = 6. This is robust: tested with failing marks all 0, all 3, a mixed set, and even all 4, the 8th value is 6 every time. RUNNER-UP: option C (7), which is the median of the ten PRINTED marks alone; it would win only if the question were read as asking for the median of the passing candidates rather than of all fifteen, which the stem explicitly does not say. Flagged because the printed count of candidates exceeds the list of marks given, but the question is answerable as printed.
Sorted: 111, 141, 154, 175, 176, 180, 191. With 7 values the median is the 4th = 175 gm.

The 'average size sold' means the size sold most often; shoe size is a discrete category whose most frequently occurring value is the mode. A mean or median size would not tell the shopkeeper which size to stock.

In a histogram the area of each rectangle is proportional to the frequency. When all class intervals have equal width the width is a common constant, so the height is directly proportional to (and taken as) the frequency of the class.

Original ages sum to 175, mean 25. After 5 years the seven members total 175 + 35 = 210. With the new member the mean is (210 + x)/8, and this exceeds the earlier mean of 25 by 1.5, i.e. equals 26.5, so 210 + x = 212 and x = 2. (The alternative reading — an increase of 1.5 over the seven-member mean of 30 after five years — gives x = 42, which matches no printed option, so only x = 2 is available.)
With b boys and 100 - b girls: 50b + 40(100 - b) = 46 × 100 gives 10b = 600, b = 60 and girls = 40. The boys exceed the girls by 60 - 40 = 20.
The algebraic sum of deviations about the arithmetic mean is always zero, since sum(x_i - xbar) = sum(x_i) - n·xbar = 0. Here the mean is 45 and the computed sum of deviations is exactly 0.
The five observations are in AP with middle term x + 4, so m = x + 4 and x = m - 4. The mean of x, x+2, x+4 is their middle term x + 2 = m - 2.
The sequence 2, 4, ..., 100 has 50 terms, so the median is the mean of the 25th and 26th terms, i.e. (50 + 52)/2 = 51.

For two numbers GM^2 = AM × HM, so 12^2 = AM × 10 and AM = 144/10 = 14.4. Consistency check: the two numbers are roots of t^2 - 28.8t + 144 = 0, namely (72 ± 12*sqrt(11))/5, which are real and positive and whose harmonic mean recomputes to exactly 10.
